episodes.160888: As an area of high pressure continued to build strength over the Great Basin area, dry air moving into New Mexico from the north continued to limit the amount of thunderstorms over the area on September 6, 2021. However, enough instability and moisture was still in place across the northeast corner of the state to allow for isolated thunderstorms, and a weak boundary draped across the area even provided enough wind shear to allow for these thunderstorms to become severe. One thunderstorm near Seneca in Union County produced one inch hail as it slowly moved southward through the county.
episodes.161194: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a strong cold front during the morning hours across east-central Wisconsin. Very large hail up to grapefruit size (4.5) fell over the Fox Valley region. The grapefruit size hail from Outagamie County was the largest on record for that county and tied for the third largest ever recorded in the state of Wisconsin.
episodes.161195: Strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds and large hail as they tracked over Lake Michigan and the bay of Green Bay during the morning hours.
episodes.161575: Light southwesterly flow coupled with abundant moisture brought widespread showers and storms to West Central Florida. Unfortunately, one of those thunderstorms produced a fatal lightning strike.
episodes.161922: There were numerous reports of large hail and damaging severe thunderstorm wind gusts on September 7th.  Wind gusts reached close to 70 mph in some areas and hail up to two and a half inches in diameter was reported.
episodes.162865: A line of severe thunderstorms developed, which led to some large hail reports for parts of northwest Illinois. Up to golf ball sized hail was reported.
episodes.162926: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of northern Illinois on September 7th, producing very large hail and localized significant wind damage.
episodes.162927: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across portions of northwest Indiana during the afternoon of September 7th.
episodes.162928: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of September 7th.
episodes.162965: A well-organized line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed early afternoon on Tuesday, September 7th, along and ahead of an advancing cold front. The  majority of the damage was observed north of I-69 in cities such as Midland and Saginaw, where extensive tree damage, power outages, and 1 hail were observed; however, less widespread reports were received south of the I-69 corridor. The line of storms farther south was followed by a swath of high winds, where sustained winds (not associated with thunderstorms) were observed to be 40-50 mph, with gusts up to 60 mph. Between the severe thunderstorms and high winds, approximately 150,000 customers lost power.
episodes.163001: Weak high pressure over the western Atlantic promoted weak southerly low-level flow across the area along with sufficient moisture. The weak flow allowed for the sea breezes to be the dominating weather pattern and storm propagator throughout the day. Both the Atlantic and Gulf sea breezes collided across the interior and Lake Okeechobee region which spurred the development of a waterspout over the Lake Okeechobee waters.
episodes.163056: A potent low level jet ahead of an advancing cold front brought a round of thunderstorms to western Lake Superior during the early morning hours of the 7th. In the wake of the cold front later in the day, a deepening surface low brought another round of storms across the lake during the afternoon and evening hours. Both rounds brought sporadic strong winds gusts to the head of the lake area.
episodes.163057: A rapidly deepening surface low and its associated cold front moved across northwest Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours. Elevated thunderstorms developed behind the cold front and a few of the storms produced sporadic damaging winds with a few downed trees and minor structure damage primarily around Lake Nebagamon.
episodes.163160: A cold front moved into northern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 7th, helping to initiate thunderstorms. Several of the thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts and hail.
episodes.163172: A line of storms moved through southern MI well ahead of a cold front. These storms produced flooding rains over northern Berrien (training), and locally damaging wind gusts and small hail from Berrien County to Hillsdale County. There was also an EF1 tornado in Hillsdale County.
episodes.163175: A broken line of thunderstorms along a cold front moved east to southeast across southern WI with numerous reports of large hail.
episodes.163179: A seasonably strong shortwave dug from the northern Great Plains into the Great Lakes by the morning of 9/7, initiating multiple lines of severe storms during the morning and early afternoon across northern Michigan. The first severe storms formed along a warm front mixing north across the CWA while a second line of stormed initiated along a cold front swinging across the state. Multiple hail reports were received with the largest stone measuring 1.75 along with damaging wind gusts experienced across the area.
episodes.163206: A lightning strike caused damage to a local power substation and caused power outages in L'anse in the early morning of the 7th.
episodes.163207: A severe thunderstorm three miles northwest of Republic downed a couple of trees in the early morning of the 7th.
episodes.163208: Strong thunderstorms moved across portions of western Lake Superior on the 7th.
episodes.163209: A cold front triggered a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms across north-central Illinois during the late afternoon and early evening of September 7th.  A supercell embedded within the line dropped golf ball-sized hail in Colfax in eastern McClean County.  Meanwhile other cells produced minor wind damage and hail up to quarter-sized.
episodes.163370: Thunderstorms moving through Saginaw Bay and southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts up to 50 knots.
episodes.163381: A potent low level jet ahead of an advancing cold front brought a round of thunderstorms to north-central Minnesota during the early morning hours of the 7th. While most of the storms remained below severe limits, one storm did produce hail to the size of nickels in Cass County.
episodes.163454: Cold advection behind Monday's thunderstorm line and cold frontal passage allowed for sufficient instability to develop over Lake Ontario for some early morning waterspouts. As the day ensued, shear increased, so while the waterspout threat diminished, the threat for gusty winds in showers increased, resulting in isolated convective wind gusts along the shoreline.
episodes.163499: Isolated severe thunderstorms impacted 3 counties in Northwest Minnesota during the late evening and early overnight period on September 6.
episodes.163519: Multiple rounds of storms crossed Lake Michigan during the morning, producing strong wind gusts in excess of 40 mph and hail over the nearshore waters.
episodes.163521: Multiple rounds of storms crossed northern Michigan during the early afternoon, eventually moving out into Lake Huron and producing strong wind gusts in excess of 40 mph.

A weak tornado developed west of the intersection of S Bunn Road and Cole/Bankers Road, and moved quickly east along the north side of the road causing areas of significant tree damage east to Cambria Road. Two 1000 lb round hay bales were picked up from a field south of Bankers Road and thrown into a ditch and yard on the north side of the road. Several power poles were snapped in the area. It appears the tornado briefly lifted after crossing Cambria Road, but touched down again on the east side of S Hillsdale Road where several outbuildings and a silo were destroyed. The tornado intensified further as it moved through the Hillsdale Golf and Country Club where considerable, widespread tree damage, including several uprooted trees, occurred. The tornado quickly weakened as it moved across Baw Beese Lake with a few tree branches damaged along Oakwood Drive. No further damage was observed past this point. Maximum winds estimated at around 100 mph (EF-1) with a maximum width of around 450 yards.
